Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: US, Asia-Pacific, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    US airstrikes on Iran have triggered a risk-off wave across global markets — oil at a 5-week high, bond yields surging (US 10Y at 4.81%, near 3-year high), and equities selling off in Asia and on Wall Street. Inflation anxiety is the central theme, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruption fears. The Fed is increasingly expected to hike 25bps at its Sep 16 meeting (67% probability, up sharply from 39.6% a week prior). RBNZ hiked as expected but struck a dovish tone. USD is firming; gold, bitcoin, and ether are marginally lower.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the bond market selloff, surging US 10Y yields, and Fed rate hike expectations are the central drivers of all market moves described)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly present — Fed hike expectations are a key narrative)
Probability of increase: 67%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (mentioned only implicitly as the alternative to a hike)
Probability of holding: 33%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (no mention or implication of a rate cut)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (Decidedly hawkish — Fed hike probability jumped from 39.6% to 67% in one week, yields are at multi-year highs, and inflation fears are freshly reignited by the geopolitical shock; no dovish offset from the Fed side)
